outlooksByWeek.2: De'Von Achane should again be featured for the Dolphins against the 49ers in Week 2. Achane recorded only 11 carries to open the year, with Miami falling behind early-something that is likely to be a weekly occurrence-but he logged five targets. In Week 1, San Francisco allowed 114 rushing yards and a touchdown plus four receptions to backs, and with Achane rarely leaving the field (88% snap share), the makings are there for a safe outing with scoring upside.

player.seasonOutlook: Achane has quickly staked his claim as one of the best running backs in the league. The 2023 third-round pick has scored either 11 or 12 touchdowns in each of his three seasons and put up a career-high 1,838 scrimmage yards in 2025. Achane's elite receiving production is nothing new (he has finished in the top five among backs in targets and receiving yards in each of the past two years), but he made another leap forward as a rusher last season, finishing fifth at the position in rushing yards. His 5.62 yards per carry is best among qualified backs since he entered the league. The 24-year-old is eyeing his third straight top-five fantasy campaign, and while that might be tricky in an overhauled Miami offense led by quarterback Malik Willis, Achane has minimal competition for touches and should easily be the offensive centerpiece. He's a solid RB1 option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Davante Adams will look to get going when the Rams face the Giants in Week 2. Adams was held to a 3-26-0 receiving line versus San Francisco in Week 1, though the Rams' offense as a whole was held in check. Adams did draw the second-most targets (six) among Los Angeles pass catchers, as he continued to draw QB Matthew Stafford's attention more than any other player besides star Puka Nacua (nine targets). The Giants largely held Dallas' passing game in check during a Week 1 win, with no Cowboys pass catcher logging more than five receptions or 44 yards.

player.seasonOutlook: Adams' first season in Los Angeles was a success, as the veteran led the wide receiver position in touchdowns for the third time in the past six seasons. His 27 end zone targets were nine more than any other player and he now sits second in that category (148) and in TDs from scrimmage (117) since entering the league in 2014. Adams' ninth-place finish in fantasy PPG marked his ninth top-10 in his past 10 seasons. Now 33 years old, he isn't targeted as much as in years past (24% target share in 2025 was his lowest since 2016), but he's the clear No. 2 behind Puka Nacua in the Rams' elite, Matthew Stafford-led offense. Adams' heavy usage near the goal line helps cement him as a fine fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jordan Addison will look to record his first reception of the year as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Addison ran the second-most routes for Minnesota in Week 1 against the Packers, but he was unable to convert on either of his two targets. Veteran quarterback Carson Wentz, who filled in for an injured Kyler Murray (concussion), relied more on tight ends T.J. Hockenson and Josh Oliver behind Justin Jefferson. This could make Addison's role remains small as long as Wentz remains under center. With that being said, the Bears' defense did allow the fourth-most PPR points to wide receivers (46.3) in Week 1, which could open up Minnesota's passing game.

player.seasonOutlook: After impressing with a 70-911-10 receiving line on 108 targets as a rookie in 2023, Addison has seen his target, reception, yardage and touchdown totals decrease each of the last two seasons. A few missed games were partially to blame for the dips, but Minnesota's quarterback woes were the main culprit in 2025, as Addison went from 10 TDs and a 65% catch rate in both 2023 and 2024 to three TDs and a 53% catch rate last season. Addison already has a pair of top-25 fantasy campaigns to his name, but it may be a stretch for him to get there in 2026 with Kyler Murray leading the Minnesota offense, not to mention Jauan Jennings' addition to the lineup. The 24-year-old is best valued as WR4/flex.

Aiyuk remains on the 49ers' roster, but is not expected to rejoin the team. The veteran receiver was out all of last season while recovering from a torn ACL and MCL suffered in October 2024. In his two full seasons prior to the injury, Aiyuk delivered back-to-back top-15 fantasy seasons, including a 2023 campaign in which he produced a career-high 1,342 yards (seventh among wide receivers) and ranked in the top five at the position in yards per reception, yards per target and yards per route run. Even prior to the 2024 injury, however, Aiyuk was underperforming, scoring zero TDs and reaching double-digit fantasy points only once in seven games. Aiyuk is still in his prime at 28 years old, but his role and effectiveness are currently unclear. He's off the fantasy radar.

Allar was selected by the Steelers in the third round of April's draft. Allar is one of the biggest quarterbacks in this rookie class and, while he has the arm to go with his frame, accuracy is a big concern. Allar was conservative during his time at Penn State (7.6 aDOT), but he still completed only 63% of his passes and averaged 7.4 yards per attempt. In 2025, he had the worst QBR in this rookie class prior to suffering a season-ending broken ankle. On the plus side, he could add value with his legs, as he posted a career 181-1,030-12 rushing line and his 8.3% scramble rate is second highest in this class. Allar will begin his career learning the ropes behind Aaron Rodgers and perhaps Mason Rudolph.

outlooksByWeek.2: Braelon Allen will look to build on a solid opener when the Jets face the Packers in Week 2. Allen had 10 carries in Week 1 under new OC Frank Reich, after totaling 18 carries in four games before injury in 2025. The volume resulted from the Jets playing with a lead, a game script that's unlikely to repeat in Week 2. Allen remains a secondary option to Breece Hall, so patience is warranted, particularly against a defense that allowed only 3.7 yards per carry in Week 1 and is more vulnerable through the air.

player.seasonOutlook: Hopes were high for Allen entering 2025, but a slow start was followed by a season-ending knee injury in Week 4. During Weeks 1-3, Allen played 28% of the Jets' snaps and totaled 67 yards and one touchdown on 16 touches. The 2024 fourth-round pick has shown he can contribute as both a rusher (110 career carries) and receiver (32 targets), but he's simply not going to see the field much as long as feature back Breece Hall is healthy. Allen, 22, has some late-round insurance stash appeal, as he'd likely start over Isaiah Davis in the event of a Hall injury and would thus find himself on the flex radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: Josh Allen appears to have the Bills' offense humming as they get set to host the Lions in Week 2. Facing a stout Texans defense last week, Allen accounted for 357 total yards and four touchdowns, against a unit he had previously struggled. No such fears should exist Thursday night, as the Lions' depleted secondary is coming off a game where they allowed 410 yards and three touchdowns.

player.seasonOutlook: Allen enters his age-30 campaign having finished each of the past six seasons no worse than second among quarterbacks in fantasy points. Despite seeing less passing volume the past two seasons (14th or lower in pass attempts both years), the 2024 NFL MVP has finished in the top 10 in passing TDs six seasons in a row and remains a major threat with his legs (top five in carries and rushing TDs among quarterbacks all eight seasons of his career). Allen's 21.4 fantasy points per game in 2025 was actually his lowest since 2019, but it was still enough to lead the position. With Joe Brady returning as playcaller and the Bills adding a No. 1 receiver in DJ Moore, Allen remains an elite fantasy quarterback.

Allen was selected by the Commanders in the sixth round of April's draft. Allen has a good size and a solid efficiency profile, having ranked seventh in this rookie class in YAC (3.35) and 10th in forced missed tackle rate (4.5) during his four seasons at Penn State. Though he out-carried fellow draft prospect Nicholas Singleton in all four seasons at PSU, Allen was less involved as a receiver (career 70-490-4 line, including a weak 5.1 YPT) and doesn't figure to get much run as a receiver in the pros. Allen is a long shot as a sixth-rounder, but he's a name to monitor considering the state of the Washington backfield (Rachaad White, Jacory Croskey-Merritt). If Allen impresses during the offseason, he could sneak onto the fantasy radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: Keenan Allen can still get open on short passes, but the 34-year-old WR's lack of big-play potential limits his fantasy relevance to deeper formats heading into the Colts' Week 2 road game against the Chiefs. Allen caught all six of his targets in his Colts debut, leading the team in receptions, but he totaled just 32 receiving yards. Expect him to post plenty of similar stat lines this season after averaging a career-low 9.6 yards per catch with the Chargers last year.

player.seasonOutlook: A 2025 seventh-round pick, Allen is set to compete with fellow second-year back Bhayshul Tuten and newcomer Chris Rodriguez Jr. for work in the Jacksonville backfield. As a rookie, Allen played 22% of the Jaguars' offensive snaps (82% of which were pass plays), but was limited to just 33 touches and failed to find the end zone or reach 4.0 fantasy points in a single game. It's likely that Tuten will operate as the Jaguars' primary back, with Rodriguez busy on early downs and short-yardage situations, and Allen used as a passing-down specialist, same as in 2025. That said, none of the three are established as lead backs, so there's an opportunity for Allen to force his way into a larger role. The 22-year-old is worth no more than a late-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Allgeier heads into a Week 2 clash against Seattle with a big role in Arizona's backfield. Allgeier logged 17 carries for 61 yards in a season-opening win against the Chargers, getting more totes and producing more yards than rookie Jeremiyah Love. It remains to be seen if that will hold true throughout the campaign, but for the time being Allgeier seems set to be heavily involved in the Cardinals' ground game. With that said, both Allgeier and Love could find the sledding tough in Week 2 versus a Seahawks defense that yielded the third-fewest rushing yards per game during the regular season last year.

player.seasonOutlook: Allgeier signed with the Cardinals during free agency. The 2022 fifth-round NFL draft pick impressed as a rookie in Atlanta, totaling 1,174 yards on 226 touches, but he hasn't come close to those marks while playing second fiddle to Bijan Robinson over the past three seasons, and he has yet to produce a top-25 fantasy campaign. Allgeier did score eight touchdowns last season, but he remains a nonfactor as a receiver, never clearing 18 catches in a season. The 26-year-old will step into a similar role in Arizona, as the primary backup and change-of-pace option behind No. 3 overall pick Jeremiyah Love. Same as in Atlanta, Allgeier has no standalone value, but he's a very good insurance stash.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mark Andrews and the Ravens host the Saints and their defense, which ranks 13th in fantasy points allowed per game (11.3) to TEs, in Week 2. Andrews caught four of his six targets for 49 yards during Baltimore's 41-23 win in the season opener. He tied with Zay Flowers (hamstring) for the team lead in targets and finished second behind him in receptions. With Flowers and a host of other receivers dealing with injuries, Andrews could be in line for additional looks as a safety net for Lamar Jackson.

player.seasonOutlook: One of fantasy's biggest mysteries, Andrews' usage has dipped substantially over the past two seasons. After finishing in the top five in fantasy PPG five seasons in a row from 2019 to 2023, Andrews slipped to eighth in 2024 (it would've been much worse if not for 11 touchdowns on 68 targets) and fell even further to 24th last season. Andrews appeared in all 17 of Baltimore's games but ranked 18th among tight ends in targets and outside the top 20 in catches and yards. The combination of a new coaching staff, a healthy Lamar Jackson and the departure of Isaiah Likely could lead to a rebound season for Andrews, but we now have two straight seasons of underperformance. The 31-year-old remains a force near the goal line (top 10 in end zone targets seven years in a row), but he's now more of a fringe TE1 than a fantasy star.

Arroyo is eyeing a Year 2 breakout after an underwhelming rookie campaign in which he played a clear second fiddle to A.J. Barner. The 2025 second-round pick was limited to 39% of the offensive snaps during the 13 games he was active. He cleared three targets in a game only once (five in Week 7) and his lone touchdown came on one of just two targets in Week 9. Arroyo was effective as a vertical target at the collegiate level, so he remains an intriguing dynasty hold, but the 23-year-old has a tough path to short-term fantasy relevance while stuck behind Barner in Seattle's low-pass-volume offense.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brandon Aubrey was surprisingly quiet in Week 1 for the Cowboys versus the Giants. With New York dominating time of possession, Aubrey did not even attempt a field goal. He also missed one of his extra points when Javonte Williams was assessed a taunting penalty following a touchdown, leading to a 48-yard PAT try. Aubrey has nowhere to go but up in Week 2 versus the Commanders, though. Washington allowed 26.5 points per game just a season ago, which was 27th in the NFL.

Elic Ayomanor caught an 11-yard touchdown in garbage time during the Titans' season opener. That was the only catch of the game for the 2025 fourth-round pick, and Ayomanor is expected to maintain a supporting role in Tennessee's underwhelming offense in Week 2 against the Eagles, keeping him well outside of the fantasy lineup conversation in most leagues. The Titans struggled to move the ball while the game was in doubt in Week 1 against the Jets, with Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson both working ahead of Ayomanor at WR.

Saquon Barkley averaged 5.5 yards per tote in Week 1 for the Eagles. Barkley rushed 15 times for 83 yards, though was held out of the end zone in the 24-22 win over Washington. Barkley should have even greater success in Week 2 versus a dismal Titans squad. Tennessee allowed 367 yards from scrimmage to the Jets in their season opener. Tennessee was torched on the ground in particular, allowing 152 rushing yards and two touchdowns.

player.seasonOutlook: Barkley is looking to rebound in his ninth NFL season (third with the Eagles) following a big step back in 2025. After producing 2,283 yards and 15 touchdowns on 378 touches in his first season with Philly, Barkley dipped to 1,413 yards and nine scores on 317 touches in 2025. Barkley fell from first among backs in fantasy points per game (22.5) to 15th (14.5). Now 29 years old, it's possible Barkley's best days are behind him, but he's still positioned as a clear feature back in a good offense that will have a healthier line and a new playcaller in Sean Mannion. Barkley is riskier than ever, but he's still worthy of mid- to back-end RB1 consideration.

outlooksByWeek.2: AJ Barner is coming off a quiet season opener as Seattle heads to Arizona in Week 2. Barner logged just two catches on two targets for 13 yards against the Patriots last Wednesday, though those two receptions were tied for second-most on the squad. Drew Lock played most of that game at QB for Seattle, and he's expected to start in Week 2 with Sam Darnold dealing with a glute injury. The Cardinals gave up seven catches for 90  yards to Chargers tight ends in a win Sunday, so Barner could be a key target for Lock.

player.seasonOutlook: Barner was a solid contributor for the Seattle offense last season. The 2024 fourth-round pick worked his way to the top of the depth chart, and although his overall volume was limited (20th among TEs in targets and yards), he found the end zone seven times and finished 14th in fantasy points (21st in PPG). The 24-year-old is a serviceable, short-range target for Sam Darnold, but even with some rushing worked in, his role in Seattle's low-volume passing offense won't allow much upside. In fact, it's possible he loses some targets to second-year TE Elijah Arroyo this season. Barner is a fringe TE2, at best.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Bass continues to be busy for the high-scoring Bills' offense as they enter a Week 2 matchup with the Lions. In Week 1, Bass made three extra points and three field goals, though none were 50-plus yards. Detroit's defense, particularly the secondary, was suspect a week ago, and the Bills should score plenty, making Bass appealing.

Rashod Bateman and the Ravens host the Saints in Week 2. Despite leading Baltimore's receivers with 53 offensive snaps, he logged just one target and did not record a reception. With Zay Flowers' (hamstring) status up in the air and rookie Ja'Kobi Lane out with a fractured wrist suffered in the opener, Bateman's opportunities to contribute could increase. Regardless of who's active, he'll aim to bounce back against New Orleans' 21st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (37.2) to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Bateman is entering his sixth season in Baltimore following an injury-plagued 2025 campaign in which he was limited to a career-low 224 receiving yards in 13 games. After scoring nine touchdowns on only 45 receptions in 2024, Bateman had "regression" written all over him entering last season, but it was worse than expected. The 2021 first-round pick saw his target share fall from 15.4% to a career-low 11.4% and his only double-digit fantasy effort came in Week 3. The 26-year-old remains second on Baltimore's depth chart behind Zay Flowers, but even in a new scheme and with a healthy Lamar Jackson under center, he's unlikely to produce his first top-35 fantasy campaign. Bateman isn't the most appealing late-round draft pick.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jake Bates will aim to stay perfect as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. Bates nailed his only field-goal attempt and all four extra points against the Saints in Week 1. The third-year player led all NFL kickers in PATs last season in Detroit's high-powered offense, so he'll hopefully stay on the field plenty in the coming weeks. Given that the Bills' defense should provide more problems for the Lions, Bates could also get more field-goal shots in what could be a tough away matchup.

Justin Jefferson will look to keep it rolling in Week 2 as Minnesota takes on the Bears. Jefferson returned to a fantasy level in Week 1 that he didn't see much of in 2025, reeling in eight of nine targets for 92 yards and two touchdowns. The star wideout also had a solid connection with veteran Carson Wentz, who came in for an injured Kyler Murray (concussion). Given that Jefferson still produced with the Vikings' QB2, he could be in line for big games no matter who lines up under center, so long as it isn't J.J. McCarthy. He'll face a Chicago defense that allowed the fourth-most PPR points to Panthers wide receivers (46.3) in Week 1.

player.seasonOutlook: After finishing in the top 10 among receivers in fantasy PPG during each of his first five seasons, Jefferson plummeted to 30th in 2025. The fall was, of course, unrelated to Jefferson's ability, as the team's quarterback woes limited the star receiver to career-low showings in yardage (1,048), touchdowns (two), catch rate (60%) and yards per target (7.4). Jefferson's fall came despite him seeing a career-high 30.1% target share and ranking in the top six at the position in targets (141) and end zone targets (15). The 27-year-old remains an elite player, but the quarterback concerns aren't fully solved, with dual-threat Kyler Murray (one receiver managed a top-25 fantasy campaign during his time as a starter in Arizona) set to work as the starter. Perhaps Murray can ignite Jefferson similar to how he did DeAndre Hopkins at times, but there's certainly some risk. Jefferson is best considered as a mid-range WR1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Derrick Henry and the Ravens play host to the Saints for their 2026 home opener in Week 2. Henry rambled for 144 yards and three TDs on 24 carries and caught his only target for 19 yards in Baltimore's 41-23 victory. Next up is a Saints defense that surrendered 165 yards and two TDs on the ground to Jahmyr Gibbs and the Lions. Henry has tallied 16 rushing TDs in consecutive years, and he's nearly a quarter of the way there already after just one game.

player.seasonOutlook: Henry continues to defy the odds, playing at a high level despite now entering his age-32 season. In 2025, he finished exactly second in the NFL in rushing yards for the fourth season in a row, and his 24 carries inside the 5-yard line were easily the most in the league. Henry leads the NFL in carries inside the 5-yard line (42) and is second in touchdowns (34) since joining Baltimore prior to the 2024 season, and he hasn't finished lower than eighth among RBs in touchdowns since 2017. Henry continues to run at a high level (his 5.20 yards per carry last season ranked fifth among qualified backs), but he's still a nonfactor as a receiver (outside the top 45 backs in targets, catches and yards last season). He remains a featured rusher in a terrific offense and is well positioned for his fifth consecutive top-eight fantasy campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: D'Andre Swift will aim to replicate a huge game as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Swift was dominant against the Panthers in Week 1, carrying the ball 18 times for 124 yards and three touchdowns. The veteran ball carrier topped any of his games in the 2025 season, showcasing that he should also benefit from a higher-scoring Chicago offense this year. He'll play a Minnesota defense that shelled Green Bay on the ground in their opener, but he has established himself more than the Packers' current RB room.

player.seasonOutlook: Swift is entering his seventh NFL season and third with Chicago. The veteran back was busy as both a rusher and receiver en route to clearing 1,300 scrimmage yards in each of his first two seasons with the Bears. Though he found the end zone 10 times and finished 17th among backs in fantasy points per game last season, Swift deferred substantial work to Kyle Monangai and is likely to be in even more of a timeshare in 2026. Still in his prime at age 27, Swift continues to play at a high level (4.87 yards per carry last season), but his role in the Chicago offense figures to limit him to low-ceiling RB2/flex production.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bhayshul Tuten is likely to get the majority of touches in Jacksonville's backfield in Week 2 against the Broncos, just as he did in the season-opening win over the Browns. Tuten turned 16 touches into 88 yards in Week 1, while Chris Rodriguez and Ameer Abdullah combined for 55 yards on 11 touches, though Rodriguez siphoned some valuable goal-line work. Denver's defense gave up the second-fewest rushing yards in the NFL last season but just allowed Chiefs RBs Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson to combine for 259 scrimmage yards and two TDs in a Week 1 loss. Tuten has RB2 upside given his prominent role in a high-powered Jaguars offense, but he's more of a flex/RB3 for Week 2 against a talented Broncos defense searching for a rebound in their home opener.

player.seasonOutlook: Tuten is positioned to take over lead-back duties in Jacksonville following the offseason departure of Travis Etienne Jr. Tuten played sparingly as a rookie, totaling 83 carries and 14 targets in 15 games. He cleared 10 touches in only one game (a 15-touch, 74-yard effort in Week 11), but he did find the end zone in all four games in which he had at least eight touches. The 2025 fourth-round pick will see some scoring regression (seven TDs on 93 touches), but he flashed in limited work, can contribute as a rusher and receiver, is working in a good offense and has only journeyman Chris Rodriguez Jr. and passing-down specialist LeQuint Allen Jr. as his competition. Tuten is still unproven, but the 23-year-old has a path to a breakout season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Marvin Harrison will look to get going in Arizona's Week 2 tilt against Seattle. Harrison notched just one catch on three targets in a season-opening win over the Chargers, though that reception did go for a robust 33 yards. With that said, the fact that he drew such a small amount of QB Jacoby Brissett's 37 targets provides some cause for concern, especially with newcomer Kendrick Bourne getting a healthy eight targets and No. 2 wideout Michael Wilson drawing seven. The Cardinals' wideout corps as a whole faces a tough challenge in the Seahawks, who didn't allow any Patriots pass catcher to exceed 51 yards in a Week 1 victory.

player.seasonOutlook: Harrison's pro career is off to a slow start after he was selected with the No. 4 overall pick back in 2024. The Ohio State product was serviceable as a rookie (885 yards and eight TDs), but he missed five full games and was limited in others en route to a 41-608-4 receiving line in 2025. Harrison has finished 41st and 39th, respectively, in fantasy PPG despite a massive role near the goal line (he's third in the NFL in end zone targets since he was drafted and finished both seasons in the top five). Harrison is only entering his prime at age 24 and perhaps he'll make a Year 3 leap with new coach Mike LaFleur calling the plays and with Kyler Murray no longer under center. Harrison performed better with Jacoby Brissett under center last season and has the raw talent to make him well worth post-hype consideration in the middle rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: DK Metcalf and the Steelers are in New England to face the Patriots in Week 2. The veteran wideout corralled four of 10 targets for 40 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-13 Week 1 win against the Falcons. He led the team in targets by four but finished third in receiving yards. Metcalf has a hypothetical advantage over Michael Pittman after playing last year with Aaron Rodgers, and there's a good chance he'll be his favorite target against New England's 21st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (33.1) to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Metcalf returns for Year 2 in Pittsburgh after a solid but unspectacular debut season. The ex-Seahawk missed two games and finished outside the top 20 receivers in targets, catches and yardage (career-low 850), but still did just enough to produce a 21st-place finish in fantasy PPG (his fifth top-25 in his last six seasons). Metcalf soaked up 11 end zone targets and is up to 107 for his career, which leads the NFL since his debut in 2019. The 28-year-old has added target competition this season in the form of Michael Pittman Jr. and rookie Germie Bernard, so while he'll certainly remain busy, a slight dip in usage is probable. Metcalf should be valued as a back-end WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Trevor Lawrence threw four touchdown passes in the first 33 minutes of Jacksonville's lopsided Week 1 win over the Browns before the Jaguars took their foot off the gas. He has 22 touchdown passes in his last eight starts, but the surging QB could face a stiffer test in a Week 2 road game against the Broncos. They boasted the NFL's third-stingiest scoring defense last season but just gave up 31 points to the Chiefs in Week 1. Lawrence has been effective enough recently to warrant starting in fantasy despite the daunting matchup, but he's unlikely to give managers a top-five performance in Week 2.

player.seasonOutlook: Lawrence is entering his sixth NFL season after a breakout 2025 in which he ranked no lower than seventh among quarterbacks in pass attempts, completions, yards and touchdowns, as well as top 10 in carries, yards and TDs. He reeled off seven consecutive top-10 fantasy outings to finish the season. Lawrence's efficiency has been fine, at best, but he continues to generate big volume, having finished in the top 10 among QBs in pass and rush attempts in each of his four full seasons. With a strong, deep group of pass catchers and Liam Coen back as playcaller, the 26-year-old is well positioned for mid-to-back-end QB1 production.

outlooksByWeek.2: Makai Lemon was listed as the No. 3 wideout for the Eagles heading into their Week 1 clash with Washington. Unfortunately, Lemon lost five yards on three catches in his NFL debut.  On the bright side, he was targeted four times and was one of only three Eagles receivers to record a catch. Better outputs lie ahead, perhaps as early as Week 2 versus Tennessee.  The Titans surrendered 215 yards passing to Geno Smith of the Jets in their opener.

player.seasonOutlook: Lemon was selected by the Eagles with the 20th overall pick of April's draft. Lemon is on the small side (5-foot-11, 192 pounds), but he posted a 3.04 YPRR (best in this rookie class) during his collegiate career, dropping only three of 190 career targets (his 1.6% drop rate also paced this class). Lemon, who aligned in the slot on 74% of his collegiate routes, posted a dominant 79-1,156-11 receiving line in 2025, while also contributing as a rusher (two TDs) and returner. With A.J. Brown now in New England, Lemon will battle Dontayvion Wicks for No. 2 work opposite DeVonta Smith. Lemon's skill set provides him with upside, but with plenty of mouths to feed in Philly's low-volume pass offense, he's best valued as a flex option in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyjae Spears had five touches to Tony Pollard's eight in Tennessee's season-opening loss. Heading into a Week 2 home game against the Eagles, the Titans once again look like one of the NFL's worst offenses. Given Spears' role as a supporting piece in Tennessee's low-octane offense, he's tough to trust as anything more than a low-end deep-league flex play. Spears has exceeded 50 scrimmage yards three times in 14 appearances since the start of last season.

player.seasonOutlook: Spears is set for his fourth NFL season, including his third as a change-of-pace backup to Tony Pollard. The role hasn't been particularly fruitful from a fantasy standpoint, as Spears has yet to clear five touchdowns in a season, nor has he produced a top-30 fantasy campaign. Spears, who has also struggled with durability (nine games missed over the past two years), isn't used much as a rusher (100 or fewer carries all three seasons), but he is an effective receiver (top 10 among RBs in catches in both 2023 and 2025). The 25-year-old will resume his role as a receiving specialist in 2026 and, even if the Titans' offense makes a big leap in QB Cam Ward's second season, Spears is unlikely to find his way to consistent fantasy value.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jake Ferguson was surprisingly quiet in Week 1 for the Cowboys versus the Giants. Ferguson finished with just two catches for six yards in the 28-20 loss. Meanwhile, fellow tight ends Brevyn Spann-Ford and Luke Schoonmaker both gained more yards through the air. However, the Dallas passing attack struggled as a whole, leaving no pass-catcher with more than 45 yards receiving in the contest. In Week 2, the Cowboys will look to rebound versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.

player.seasonOutlook: Ferguson has emerged as a reliable target for Dak Prescott in the high-scoring Dallas offense, which has led to solid fantasy production. Ferguson, who has handled a 17% target share each of the past three seasons, is fresh off a career year in which he ranked third among tight ends in receptions, touchdowns and end zone targets (10). His nine top-12 fantasy weeks tied for second, though it's worth noting that his production dropped off substantially with a healthy CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens on the field during the second half of the season (under 12.0 fantasy points in each of his final eight healthy games, 7.3 PPG during the span). The 27-year-old's role as a short-range target (4.7 aDOT last season) limits his yardage upside, but he sees just enough work, including near the goal line, to allow fringe-TE1 production. Don't call him "Joke Farterson" ("Fantasy Football Now" viewers get it); Ferguson is vying for his third top-10 fantasy campaign in his past four seasons.

outlooksByWeek.2: Eddy Pineiro heads into a Week 2 matchup versus Miami on the heels of making two field goals in San Francisco's season-opening victory against the Rams. Pineiro's makes came from 20 and 56 yards out, though he also missed a 52-yarder. The veteran kicker made a career-high six FGs from 50-plus yards out last year, so San Francisco is clearly comfortable relying on his leg from that distance. The 49ers could put up plenty of points in Week 2, as the Dolphins just gave up 27 points to Las Vegas in a Week 1 loss.

Malachi Fields tied for third on the Giants in targets in Week 1. Fields caught two passes for 25 yards on four targets in his debut. Only Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely had more targets. The Giants are rather thin at wideout behind the aforementioned Nabers, and Fields is a huge target at 6-4, 225-lbs, so expect him to continue to be a decent contributor to the revamped offense. In Week 2, the G-Men will face a Rams defense that allowed 205 passing yards and three passing scores in a lackluster season-opener.

player.seasonOutlook: Fields was selected by the Giants in the third round of April's draft. One of the biggest and strongest receivers in this rookie class, Fields figures to work as a perimeter, vertical target in the pros (career 13.3 aDOT during 49 collegiate games). Fields, who dropped just seven passes in college, handled a target share of, at least, 20% and air yard share of, at least, 30% during each of his final three collegiate seasons (two at Virginia, one at Notre Dame). Fields will battle Darnell Mooney and Darius Slayton for New York's No. 2 receiver gig behind Malik Nabers. The rookie is a fine late-round flier.

Zak Kuhr, elevated to the defensive coordinator position early last season, steered this D/ST to the sixth-most fantasy points and a Super Bowl LX berth. Now in the permanent role, he'll have a strengthened unit, with DE Dre'Mont Jones and S Kevin Byard brought on board, though it's fair to point out that the 2025 Patriots generated nearly one quarter of their fantasy points on defensive or special teams touchdowns. This is a team better used as a streaming than weekly defense, and bear in mind it has a tough-as-nails Super Bowl rematch in Seattle to begin the year.

outlooksByWeek.2: Sam Darnold suffered a soft-tissue glute injury in Seattle's season-opening win and isn't likely to play in Week 2 against Arizona. As a result, Drew Lock is in line to guide the Seahawks' offense. Darnold isn't expected to miss significant time and could be back as soon as Week 3.

player.seasonOutlook: Darnold's first season with the Super Bowl champion Seahawks couldn't have gone much better from a real-life standpoint, but it simply didn't translate to much fantasy success. Despite finishing fifth in the NFL in passing yards for the second season in a row, Darnold finished 27th in fantasy points per game. He was very boom or bust, delivering seven top-10 weeks but also nine finishes outside the top 20. Turnovers (15 INTs were second most in the NFL) and a lack of rushing were the culprits. The 29-year-old will have a new playcaller in Brian Fleury, but otherwise it's roughly the status quo offensively. Darnold is no more than a fringe QB2 with a limited ceiling.

outlooksByWeek.2: Antonio Williams led the Commanders in receiving in Week 1 despite playing just 26 offensive snaps. Williams ended up with four catches for 64 yards and a touchdown in his NFL premiere. He had as many targets as Terry McLaurin. Williams should see the field with increasing frequency if he continues to perform this well. He has a favorable matchup in Week 2 versus a Dallas defense that was the worst in the NFL last season, and surrendered three passing scores in the season-opening loss to the Giants.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams was selected by the Commanders in the third round of April's draft. He is an undersized slot receiver (75% slot in his collegiate career) who soaked up 208 catches (fourth most in this rookie class) during his four seasons (43 games) at Clemson. He was primarily a short-range option (8.0 aDOT), but he caught a healthy 75% of his targets and added value as a rusher (career 25-187-2 rushing), punt returner and even as a passer (143 yards and two TDs on four attempts). Williams is in an all-out battle with the likes of Dyami Brown, Luke McCaffrey, Jaylin Lane and Treylon Burks for the No. 3 WR gig behind Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs. He's worth no more than a late pick in deep leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: James Cook will seek higher volume when the Bills face the Lions in Week 2. Cook logged just 13 carries in a surprisingly high-scoring opener in Houston, going for 57 yards while adding three catches on four targets but failing to reach the end zone after scoring 32 times over the last two seasons. Detroit's defense allowed a fair 4.0 yards per carry last week but is far more vulnerable through the air. Cook's bulk role is unquestioned, keeping his floor stable while a potential shootout creates more chances for him to reach pay dirt.

player.seasonOutlook: Cook signed a contract extension last offseason and was immediately vaulted into the biggest role of his career. The 2022 second-round NFL draft pick finished in the top five among backs in carries, rushing yards (league-high 1,621), touchdowns and yards per carry (5.25). The one limiting factor in Cook's fantasy output was a minimal receiving role (his 40 targets ranked 26th among RBs), but he still came through with a sixth-place finish in fantasy points. The 26-year-old is set to play the same role in Joe Brady's scheme and will be a candidate for his third straight double-digit touchdown campaign as long as Josh Allen is under center. Consider Cook a midrange RB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brock Bowers sat out the Raiders' season-opening win over the Dolphins after undergoing minor knee surgery just before the start of the campaign. The star tight end isn't expected to be out for long, and in his absence Michael Mayer will top the team's depth chart at the position, although running back Ashton Jeanty may have been the biggest beneficiary in terms of production against Miami. If Bowers is cleared to return in Week 2, he'll be facing a Chargers defense that finished fifth in PPR points allowed to TEs in 2025, although it couldn't contain Trey McBride to begin the current campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Bowers entered 2025 with high expectations and appeared well on his way to another productive season with 103 yards in Week 1, but a late-game injury limited him for three weeks and led to five full missed games. Bowers remained productive when healthy, finishing second among tight ends in fantasy PPG. Incredibly, he tied for fifth in the NFL with 13 end zone targets despite all the missed action. Bowers, who posted a 112-1,194-5 receiving line as a rookie in 2024, will be the top target for No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza. The 23-year-old is well positioned for a highly productive season and should be on your radar in the second or third round.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylen Waddle did not contribute much in his Broncos' debut, catching just one of three targets for a meager two yards in the Week 1 loss to Kansas City. Steve Spagnuolo's rebuilt secondary prioritized taking Waddle out of the picture, and the former Dolphin wideout hasn't yet established enough chemistry with QB Bo Nix to overcome consistent double teams. Waddle will look to bounce back in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that was tied for 17th last season in points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Waddle was traded to Denver after spending his first five seasons in Miami. The 2021 first-round pick was solid during his Dolphins tenure, finishing in the top 30 among receivers in fantasy PPG four times, though never reaching the top 10 while often playing second fiddle to Tyreek Hill. Although he has been a reliable target and has missed only seven games in five years, Waddle hasn't finished a season higher than 20th in targets or catches since 2021. In Denver, the 27-year-old Waddle will compete with Courtland Sutton for the team lead in targets in a scheme that likes to spread the ball around. Not utilized near the goal line much at 5-foot-10 and 180 pounds (he's yet to clear seven end zone targets in a season), Waddle is likely to max out as a back-end WR2 in Denver.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tee Higgins and the Bengals visit the Texans for a Week 2 battle between two playoff hopefuls. He caught three of six targets for 59 yards during Cincinnati's season-opening victory. Higgins tied for second on the team in receptions and targets while finishing behind Mike Gesicki for the lead in receiving yards. He draws a favorable matchup against Houston's 26th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (41.5) to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Higgins may be overshadowed by teammate Ja'Marr Chase, but that hasn't stopped the veteran receiver from playing a key role near the goal line in the Bengals' pass-friendly offense. Despite missing seven games over the past two seasons, Higgins sits eighth among receivers in end zone targets (24) and fourth in touchdowns (21) during the span. The 2020 second-round pick finished both seasons in the top 20 in fantasy points (overall and per game). Durability (he hasn't played a full season since 2020) and a limited target share are concerns here, but Higgins' combination of talent and role in a Joe Burrow-led offense are enough to allow fringe-WR2 production.

outlooksByWeek.2: Terry McLaurin had a rough Week 1 for the Commanders. On only four targets, McLaurin caught a mere two passes for 14 yards in the 24-22 loss to the Eagles. Meanwhile, both Stefon Diggs and rookie Antonio Williams found the end zone in their respective debuts for Washington. It will be interesting to see if the presence of Diggs in particular impacts McLaurin, as Diggs more than doubled McLaurin in targets with nine. Both wideouts should see plenty of action in Week 2 versus a poor Cowboys defense, though. Dallas allowed 229 passing yards and three touchdowns through the air to Jaxson Dart in their season opener.

player.seasonOutlook: McLaurin is eyeing a bounce-back campaign following a lost 2025 season in which both he (seven missed games) and quarterback Jayden Daniels (10 missed games) were sidelined for extended periods. The dud season came after Daniels helped McLaurin to a career year in 2024, which included 13 touchdowns (second most among WRs) and a seventh-place finish in fantasy points. McLaurin's target ceiling remains a concern (he's been in the 21-25% target share range each of his seven seasons), but with his quarterback healthy and his role as a vertical threat in new playcaller David Blough's offense, McLaurin is certainly poised for a rebound. The 30-year-old is best valued as a mid-to-back-end WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 2 matchup against the Patriots. He rushed eight times for 15 yards and caught two of five targets for another six yards during Pittsburgh's Week 1 20-13 win over Atlanta. Dowdle's backfield partner, Jaylen Warren, was much more efficient with his 15 touches, which he turned into 73 scrimmage yards. It will be difficult to trust Dowdle in a tilt versus New England's 14th-ranked defense, which has allowed 84 rushing yards to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Dowdle signed with the Steelers after nearly identical campaigns with the Cowboys in 2024 (1,328 yards and five TDs on 274 touches) and Panthers in 2025 (1,373 yards and seven TDs on 275 touches). He was effective as a rusher (4.57 yards per carry) and fairly busy as a receiver (50 targets both years) en route to finishing just inside the top 25 in fantasy points per game both seasons. Now in Pittsburgh, the 28-year-old is expected to share work with Jaylen Warren. Earning lead-rusher duties could get Dowdle into the weekly flex discussion, but the ceiling will be low and he'll likely need an injury in order to find his way to consistent fantasy output. Consider him for your bench.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jordan Mason will be out for Week 2 as the Vikings take on the Bears. Mason hurt his thumb after week one against the Packers, and he's now been placed on IR for the injury. The fifth-year running back (30 of 65 offensive snaps) and Aaron Jones (29 snaps) had a near-even split of the backfield reps against the Packers, with Mason leading the ground attack with 59 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries. Unfortunately, Mason will now be out for at least the next four weeks, priming Jones for a bigger role moving forward.

player.seasonOutlook: Mason is back for his second season in Minnesota and will battle 31-year-old Aaron Jones Sr. for backfield opportunities. Mason's role was almost exactly as expected last season, as he was utilized often as a rusher (9.9 carries per game), but a nonfactor as a receiver (1.0 targets per game). Mason reached 13 fantasy points just once in his 16 games and it was a 23.6-point effort in Week 3, one of five games Jones missed. Mason, 27, is an effective rusher -- his 5.10 YPC ranks third and his 2.42 YAC second among 54 RBs with 350-plus carries since he entered the league -- but adding so little as a receiver (34 career targets) severely limits his fantasy output. Even if Jones were to miss time, Mason would max out as a flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Matthew Stafford and the Rams will look to bounce back from a rough season-opening loss when they face the Giants in Week 2. Stafford threw for just 155 yards with no TDs and one interception against San Francisco last Thursday. He did still manage to connect with favorite target Puka Nacua five times for 74 yards, but no other Rams pass catcher had more than 26 yards in the defeat. A matchup with the Giants awaits, but New York had good results against Dallas' passing game in Week 1, holding QB Dak Prescott to 175 yards with one interception, albeit with two TDs.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning NFL MVP, Stafford returns for his 18th NFL season and his fifth with the Rams. The 38-year-old is fresh off an elite season in which he led the NFL in passing yards and touchdowns, which allowed him nine top-10 fantasy weeks (tied for third most at the position). Stafford's third-place finish in fantasy points per game was his first top-10 finish since 2019, and some regression is likely due to a complete lack of rushing (65 or fewer rushing yards in five straight seasons and one rushing touchdown since 2017). Stafford still has receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams and a strong offensive line at his disposal, so another big passing season is possible. That's just enough to keep him in the fringe QB1 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: Woody Marks is set to occupy a change-of-pace role behind David Montgomery in Week 2, when the Texans host the Bengals. Marks turned 11 touches into 40 scrimmage yards in Week 1 against the Bills, while Montgomery had 79 yards and three TDs on 23 touches. Cincinnati had the worst run defense in the league last season, but Marks' modest usage makes him no better than a deep-league flex play as long as Montgomery is healthy.

player.seasonOutlook: Marks, a fourth-round NFL draft pick in 2025, played a substantial role as a rookie, soaking up 220 touches (22nd among RBs), but he struggled with efficiency (his 3.59 yards per carry and 1.61 yards after contact both ranked near the basement) and found the end zone only five times. The result was 9.4 fantasy points per game and one top-10 fantasy outing. Marks appears ticketed for a lesser role in 2026 now that David Montgomery was brought in to serve as the likely leader of a backfield committee. Especially in an offense that doesn't use backs in the passing game very much, Marks is no more than a bench/insurance stash.

outlooksByWeek.2: Michael Mayer led the Raiders in targets with seven in a season-opening win over the Dolphins, although he turned that volume into just six catches for 32 yards. That opportunity came as Brock Bowers was sidelined following minor knee surgery, and while the third-year star isn't expected to be out long, he has yet to be cleared for Week 2. If Mayer does get the start at tight end, he'll be facing a Chargers defense that finished fifth in points allowed to TEs last year, although it couldn't contain Trey McBride to begin the current campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Mayer enters his first contract year expected to resume his role as Las Vegas' oft-utilized No. 2 TE behind Brock Bowers. The 2023 second-round pick has yet to come close to playing a full season, nor has he emerged as a reliable fantasy option. Last season, he averaged 2.9 targets and 3.4 fantasy points in nine games with Bowers, compared to 6.0 targets and 10.9 PPG in the four games in which Bowers was sidelined. A short-range target (career 5.5 aDOT) with minimal goal line work (one career end zone target), Mayer is way off the fantasy radar. He should be added to rosters only if Bowers misses time.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kendrick Bourne had a promising performance for Arizona in Week 1 and will look to be productive again versus the Seahawks in Week 2. Bourne led Cardinals wideouts with eight catches and 75 yards in a season-opening victory versus the Chargers, with only stud tight end Trey McBride outpacing his eight targets. The veteran Bourne looked to have great rapport with QB Jacoby Brissett, so it will be interesting to see how the target distribution shakes out in Week 2 and beyond. He won't have an easy matchup against Seattle, who limited New England to 178 yards through the air in a Week 1 win.

Kalif Raymond could continue to be a consistent option as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Raymond benefited from a high-scoring Week 1 win, reeling in eight of nine targets for 84 yards. The veteran wide receiver was also on the field for 60 percent of offensive snaps, so it appears at least a WR3 role is cemented moving forward. He'll face a Minnesota defense that ceded the second-most PPR points (55.2) to his position this past Sunday.

player.seasonOutlook: Raheem Morris comes aboard as the 49ers' defensive coordinator this season, and between questions about his scheme's fit to the team's personnel and the injuries that have struck this roster in recent years, it's tough to get fully behind a rebound from this D/ST. An opening-week road matchup with the Rams should make this a no-go draft day pick, but the 49ers could have their matchup moments later in the year.

outlooksByWeek.2: C.J. Stroud has turned the ball over nine times in Houston's last three games, dating back to the start of last season's playoffs. He'll face a Bengals defense in Week 2 that just forced three turnovers from Buccaneers QB Baker Mayfield. Stroud threw for 274 yards and two TDs in Week 1 against the Bills but fumbled away Houston's chance to win the game in the final minute. The Texans' vaunted defense faces another tough test against Joe Burrow and the Bengals, so Stroud and the offense will be relied upon to keep pace. Stroud is a viable fantasy option in superflex or two-QB formats but ranks outside the starting range in single-QB leagues.

player.seasonOutlook: Stroud enters his fourth NFL season yet to emerge as a quality fantasy option and having seen his passing production dip during each season of his career. Stroud impressed as a rookie with 24 passing TDs, three rushing TDs and a ninth-place finish in fantasy points per game (18.4). During the past two seasons, he failed to clear 20 passing touchdowns, has a total of one rushing TD and averaged 13.8 points, ranking outside the top 20 both years. Stroud's efficiency has been solid at best and thanks in part to Houston's elite defense, he hasn't needed to throw the ball (or scramble) very often. There's little reason to expect much change in 2026, so even with a good, deep group of pass catchers, the 24-year-old is best viewed as a low-upside, fringe QB2 in 12-team leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Carson Wentz could be in line to start again as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Wentz came in for an injured Kyler Murray (concussion) against the Packers in Week 1, and he ended up delivering a come-from-behind win. The veteran completed 12 of 19 passes for 133 yards and three touchdowns, and he did not commit a turnover during the matchup. If Murray is unable to clear concussion protocol ahead of Sunday, Wentz will be in position to get his first start since 2025 against a Bears defense that gave up 361 passing yards, three touchdowns and one interception to Bryce Young in their opener.

Trey Smack will look to stay solid as the Packers take on the Jets in Week 2. Smack converted all three of his field-goal attempts against the Vikings in Week 1, but he did go 1-for-2 on XPAs. Still, the perfect field-goal percentage outshines his one miss. Smack will face a Jets defense that allowed a bottom-five fantasy points (4.0) total to Titans kicker Joey Slye this past Sunday.

Amon-Ra St. Brown will aim to keep it rolling as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. St. Brown kicked off the season with a bang against the Saints, catching 10 of 14 targets for 67 yards and two touchdowns. The star wide receiver continues to hold the monopoly in Detroit's passing game, and his production doesn't look to be taking a dip any time soon. He'll take on a Bills defense that ceded a seventh-most PPR points to Houston wide receivers (40.0) in Week 1.

player.seasonOutlook: The only player in NFL history with 90-plus catches in each of his first five NFL seasons, St. Brown continues to assert himself as one of the league's best players. The 2021 fourth-round pick has finished exactly third among receivers in fantasy points three seasons in a row, ranking no lower than fourth in catches, yards and touchdowns each year. St. Brown actually enjoyed a career-high target share in 2025 (31.6%), which helped him to 13 top-20 fantasy outings. The 26-year-old has no added target competition and remains Jared Goff's clear No. 1 target. He should be off the board in the first round of your draft.

outlooksByWeek.2: Nico Collins is in danger of sitting out against the Bengals in Week 2 due to a hamstring injury. He paced Houston's passing attack with a 7-75-1 line on 10 targets in the season opener, so he would work as the team's WR1 again in Week 2 against the Bengals if given the green light to suit up. Cincinnati didn't allow a passing TD to the Buccaneers in Week 1 but had one of the league's worst all-around defenses last season, when the Bengals gave up the second-most yards and third-most points in the NFL. Collins remains a set-and-forget fantasy WR1 as he chases his fourth consecutive 1,000-yard receiving season.

player.seasonOutlook: Collins heads into his sixth NFL campaign yet to play a full 17-game season, but having been very productive when on the field. The 2021 third-round pick has cleared 1,000 yards and scored either seven or eight touchdowns each of the past three seasons, finishing in the top 10 in fantasy PPG and top 12 in yards per route run in all three. A force near the goal line, Collins ranked fourth among receivers with 13 end zone targets in 2025. The 27-year-old's target share doesn't stack up with other top receivers (he has never cleared 24.4%), but his high-end efficiency is just enough to keep him in the back-end WR1 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Olave is expected to remain the Saints' top wideout in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Olave definitely benefitted from Tyler Shough's 56 pass attempts during the Week 1 overtime loss. However, New Orleans averaged 34.8 pass attempts per game in 2025, so Olave will likely continue to see loads of volume. Additionally, he saw a 25 percent target share, which should remain steady until Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) returns later this season. Olave is in for a tough matchup this week, however, with Baltimore's defense allowing just 25.0 PPR fantasy points to WRs in Week 1.

player.seasonOutlook: Olave is fresh off a career year in which he reached new highs in targets (156), receptions (100), yardage (1,163) and touchdowns (nine). He finished eighth among receivers in fantasy PPG, which beat out his previous career best of 19th in 2023. Olave finished no lower than seventh among receivers in nearly every counting stat, including end zone targets (12) and air yards (1,816). The big season was a sigh of relief after a 2024 campaign riddled with concussions, and it positions the 26-year-old right back in the fringe-WR1 discussion. Especially with No. 8 overall pick Jordyn Tyson expected to miss a month or two with a hamstring injury, Olave will remain Tyler Shough's top target, and that sets him up for another highly productive campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens host the Saints for an interconference showdown in Week 2. Jackson was stellar in the opener despite losing a fumble, throwing for 324 yards (17-for-25) with one TD and no picks while rushing seven times for another 40 yards and a TD. Although he still offers elite upside at the QB position, it's important to note that his favorite receiver, Zay Flowers, is dealing with a hamstring injury that coach Jesse Minter considers "day-to-day." The two connected on five of six targets for 150 yards and a score in the victory. The New Orleans defense ranks 12th in fantasy points allowed per game (18.5) to QBs after Jared Goff's 206 yards and two TDs in Week 1.

player.seasonOutlook: Jackson, 29, is eyeing a rebound after a disappointing, injury-plagued 2025. Jackson started the season strong (26-plus fantasy points in each of his first three games) but left Week 4 because of an injury and wasn't the same once he returned in Week 9 (13.5 fantasy points per game in his final nine outings). Jackson's overall rushing was down, but that was likely a product of him not being fully healthy, especially considering his scramble rate (8.4%) remained high. Jackson has a new coach (Jesse Minter) and playcaller (Declan Doyle), but his supporting cast is otherwise similar to a 2024 campaign in which he paced all quarterbacks in fantasy points. Assuming he's back to full health, Jackson is a strong bet for a rebound and should be valued as a high-end QB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rhamondre Stevenson will look for a heavier workload when the Patriots face the Steelers in Week 2. Stevenson notched 23 touches to open the year, and despite the potential return of TreVeyon Henderson (ankle), Stevenson should handle early-down work at a minimum. He's mainly an accumulator, averaging 4.0 yards per carry or less in two of the previous three seasons and just 2.8 to open 2026. But volume is king, and Stevenson likely has that since he also catches passes out of the backfield. Pittsburgh was vulnerable in Week 1 to receiving backs, plus Stevenson likely handles goal-line work, making him intriguing even in a difficult spot against a defense that allowed 3.8 yards per carry to open the year.

player.seasonOutlook: Stevenson will battle with second-year back TreVeyon Henderson for touches in the New England backfield. The duo shared the backfield at times last season, but it was the veteran Stevenson who usually operated as the lead back. He earned the role, ranking fifth among backs in forced missed tackle rate, per PFF, second in yards after contact (2.82) and first in yards per target (9.1). Stevenson, who is entering his sixth season, did miss three games (he has missed time three seasons in a row), and his overall volume was limited (9.3 carries and 2.7 targets per game), which led to a 25th-place finish in fantasy points. Now 28 years old and with Henderson still very much in the mix, Stevenson, who has one top-20 fantasy campaign to his name, is a low-upside bench option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tony Pollard got just eight touches in the season opener as the Titans fell behind against the Jets and abandoned the run. Negative game scripts could be a recurring problem for Pollard, and the Titans will be substantial Week 2 underdogs at home against the Eagles. On the bright side, Pollard recorded at least 1,288 scrimmage yards in each of the previous two seasons, even as the Titans posted a 3-14 record both years. Pollard's status as the team's starting running back keeps him in the Week 2 flex/RB3 conversation.

player.seasonOutlook: Pollard has handled a hefty 67.2% of the Titans' designed rushing attempts since his arrival two seasons ago (15.2 per game) and, even with solid efficiency, he has finished 22nd and 30th in fantasy points per game. The culprits? Tennessee's struggling offense (Pollard has exactly five TDs in both seasons) and a limited receiving role when Tyjae Spears has been healthy (Pollard's targets fell from 3.5 per game in 2024 to 2.5 per game in 2025). Barring a major leap from quarterback Cam Ward, Pollard is unlikely to deliver only the second top-20 fantasy campaign (in points per game) of his career. The 29-year-old, entering his eighth NFL season (third with Tennessee), is a low-ceiling flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Harold Fannin and the Browns visit the Buccaneers in Week 2, facing the 30th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (25.1) to TEs. The second-year pro managed two catches on three targets for 21 yards during Cleveland's 34-10 loss in the season opener. Fannin has the perfect chance at a rebound performance against Tampa Bay, as Cincinnati's Mike Gesicki cooked their defense with five receptions for 78 yards and a TD in Week 1. Even with poor quarterback play, Fannin has the talent and opportunity as the focal point of an offense that might not be good but will be forced to throw the ball plenty while playing from behind.

player.seasonOutlook: Fannin is a rising star at the tight end position after overcoming the presence of David Njoku and a quarterback merry-go-round to produce a 72-731-6 receiving line (plus 7-13-1 rushing) as a 21-year-old rookie last season. The third-round pick's 108 targets rank eighth all time by a rookie tight end, and he finished no lower than eighth at the position in catches, yards, touchdowns and fantasy points last season. Fannin figures to see some touchdown regression (seven TDs, 3.8 expected, three end zone targets) and Cleveland still has quarterback question marks, but with Njoku gone, Fannin has a path to improve a bit on what was already a healthy 22% target share. He's a solid TE1 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rachaad White found himself on the losing end of the timeshare out of the backfield in Week 1 for Washington.  White had seven carries for 22 yards, while fellow rusher Jacory Croskey-Merritt managed 16 carries for 63 yards and a touchdown. White only had one more reception than Croskey-Merritt as well. In Week 2, Washington has a favorable matchup with the Cowboys, as Dallas allowed 165 rushing yards on the ground to the Giants in their season opener.

player.seasonOutlook: White signed with the Commanders after spending his first four seasons with the Buccaneers. The 2022 third-round pick operated as a feature back in 2023 (he finished in the top five among backs in touches, yards and fantasy points), but he played a situational role during his other three seasons. White is fine as a rusher, but he's a standout as a receiver. He's the only back in the NFL with 40-plus catches in each of the past four seasons, and his 89.1% career catch rate is easily best in NFL history among players with 100-plus targets. The 27-year-old is the favorite to lead the Washington backfield, but Jacory Croskey-Merritt and perhaps others will be involved. White will find himself on the weekly flex radar as long as he remains atop the depth chart.

outlooksByWeek.2: Josh Downs is hard to trust as anything more than a deep-league flex for the Colts' Week 2 trip to Kansas City. His four targets in the Week 1 loss to Baltimore tied for fourth on the team with Jonathan Taylor, as Daniel Jones threw more frequently to Alec Pierce, Keenan Allen and Tyler Warren. In 17 appearances since the start of last season, Downs is averaging a pedestrian 35.5 receiving yards per game in the Colts' run-heavy offense.

player.seasonOutlook: Downs has settled in as a serviceable slot receiver, which has helped him to finish in the 35-to-45 range among WRs in total fantasy points in each of his three NFL seasons. Downs peaked with a 72-803-5 receiving line in 2024, but took a step back in a crowded offense last season, and failed to deliver a single fantasy week better than 15th at the position. The undersized Downs isn't an option near the goal line, as he hasn't cleared five touchdowns or three end zone targets in a single season. The 25-year-old has a path to a slightly larger role in 2026 with Michael Pittman Jr. gone, leaving Alec Pierce, Tyler Warren and Keenan Allen as his primary target competition. Downs is a sleeper for flex production in PPR formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jalen Coker (ankle) will look to continue shining in Carolina's Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. Coker has shown out in the Panthers last two games (including their wild-card loss to end last season), having recorded a combined 17 receptions for 272 yards and three touchdowns. He's outproduced 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year Tetairoa McMillan and looks to be a major part of Carolina's offense going forward. However, Coker is dealing with an ankle issue and could struggle against a tough Falcons defense that gave up just 5.0 yards per pass attempt in Week 1, the fourth-best mark in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: After missing nearly the entire first half of 2025, Coker passed Xavier Legette and took on a larger offensive role opposite Tetairoa McMillan. From Week 8 onward (11 games, including the playoffs), Coker played 73% of the snaps and handled a 17.8% target share. The fantasy output was inconsistent (below 11.5 points in seven games), but he peaked down the stretch (more than 14 points in four of his final six, including a 9-134-1 showing against the Rams in the playoffs). Coker's strong finish is encouraging, though his rookie season went similarly (14-plus points three times, but under 11 in the other nine games). A healthy 2026 could get Coker to the next level, but flex production is his likely ceiling as long as McMillan is commanding one-quarter (if not more) of the targets in Carolina's Bryce Young-led offense.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Allgeier heads into a Week 2 clash against Seattle with a big role in Arizona's backfield. Allgeier logged 17 carries for 61 yards in a season-opening win against the Chargers, getting more totes and producing more yards than rookie Jeremiyah Love. It remains to be seen if that will hold true throughout the campaign, but for the time being Allgeier seems set to be heavily involved in the Cardinals' ground game. With that said, both Allgeier and Love could find the sledding tough in Week 2 versus a Seahawks defense that yielded the third-fewest rushing yards per game during the regular season last year.

player.seasonOutlook: Allgeier signed with the Cardinals during free agency. The 2022 fifth-round NFL draft pick impressed as a rookie in Atlanta, totaling 1,174 yards on 226 touches, but he hasn't come close to those marks while playing second fiddle to Bijan Robinson over the past three seasons, and he has yet to produce a top-25 fantasy campaign. Allgeier did score eight touchdowns last season, but he remains a nonfactor as a receiver, never clearing 18 catches in a season. The 26-year-old will step into a similar role in Arizona, as the primary backup and change-of-pace option behind No. 3 overall pick Jeremiyah Love. Same as in Atlanta, Allgeier has no standalone value, but he's a very good insurance stash.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Shough will lead the Saints' offense into a tough Week 2 matchup against the Ravens, whose defense gave up just 12.7 fantasy points to quarterbacks in Week 1. Despite a poor first half, Shough threw for 410 yards and three touchdowns in last week's overtime loss, making him the league's leading passer. However, Shough was prone to turnovers, throwing two interceptions and losing a fumble, which is something Baltimore could capitalize on. It'll be a tough Week 2 matchup, as the Ravens allowed just 166 passing yards in Week 1.

player.seasonOutlook: One of the surprise second-half breakout players of 2025, Shough scored 17-plus fantasy points in seven of his nine full games, including six straight to end the season. The 2025 second-round pick was a solid producer with his arm (250.1 passing yards per game) and his legs (19.3 rushing yards per game and three TDs). Shough didn't show a high ceiling (he never reached 22 fantasy points in a game), though that can be traced to a shaky supporting cast. That's an area that should be better in 2026 with Travis Etienne Jr. and No. 8 overall pick Jordyn Tyson (once healthy) joining the team. He's still unproven, but Shough enters Year 2 (same as coach Kellen Moore) as an intriguing fantasy breakout candidate. He's worth a look in the later rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Loop and the Ravens look to keep rolling at home versus the Saints in Week 2. Baltimore put up 41 points in their Week 1 victory, and Loop was a perfect 7-for-7 on his attempts. He made all five PATs and drilled both field-goal attempts-one from 57 yards out and one from 45. As long as he's the starting kicker, Loop should see plenty of scoring chances in this high-scoring Ravens offense. He'll try to stay perfect against a New Orleans defense that gave up 31 points to the Lions in the season opener.

player.seasonOutlook: Chris O'Leary takes the helm as Chargers defensive coordinator, a year after this unit finished 11th in fantasy points (119). With stars like Khalil Mack, Derwin James Jr. and Tuli Tuipulotu on the roster, the Chargers should again put forth solid defensive numbers, health willing. But the biggest advantage here is the team's first-two-weeks' schedule: The Chargers host the Cardinals and Raiders, two of the most favorable D/ST matchups. Just beware that things get far tougher from there (@BUF, @SEA, DEN, @KC the next four weeks).

outlooksByWeek.2: Dontayvion Wicks made his presence felt in his Eagles debut in Week 1. Wicks reeled in two passes for 73 yards and a touchdown in the 24-22 win over Washington. Only Dallas Goedert had more receiving yards than Wicks for the game. Wicks also notched four targets in his premiere for the Birds. In Week 2, Wicks will face a dismal Titans defense. Tennessee allowed 30 passing scores a season ago, which was tied for 23rd in the NFL

player.seasonOutlook: Wicks was traded to the Eagles after spending his first three NFL seasons in Green Bay. The 2023 fifth-round pick was limited to situational work during his Packers tenure, never finishing a season among the top 50 receivers in snaps, routes, targets, catches or yards. Wicks flashed at times (exactly one game of 24-plus points in each season), but otherwise scored 5.3 PPG. Even after the Eagles traded A.J. Brown, Wicks' path to targets may not be any easier in Philly. DeVonta Smith, Dallas Goedert and Saquon Barkley are all assured substantial roles, with first-round rookie Makai Lemon and Hollywood Brown also very much in the mix. Wicks, 25, will need to win the team's No. 2 receiver gig in order to have any shot at weekly flex consideration. He's barely worth late-round consideration in deep leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals take on the Texans, who ranked 26th in fantasy points allowed per game (41.5) to WRs in Week 2. After a two-catch, 12-yard dud in the season opener, he'll be aiming for a big bounce-back performance against a vulnerable secondary. Chase logged just four targets in Week 1 despite 35 pass attempts from Joe Burrow. The QB-WR duo should be primed for a rebound against a Houston defense that gave up 409 total yards at home last week.

player.seasonOutlook: Chase is fresh off yet another elite fantasy season and he's now finished four of his five NFL campaigns no lower than fifth in fantasy PPG (the exception was 11th in 2023). Chase actually saw a big dip in yardage (1,740 to 1,426), TDs (17 to 8) and fantasy PPG (23.7 to 19.6) from 2024 to 2025 (which was no surprise with Joe Burrow missing nine games), but still put up big numbers thanks to pacing the league in pass routes and targets for the second season in a row. In fact, Chase's 125 receptions make him the third receiver in NFL history with 125-plus catches in multiple seasons. The 26-year-old remains the top target in a high-scoring Bengals offense, and is one of the top players in all of fantasy.

outlooksByWeek.2: Breece Hall will look to remain busy when the Jets face the Packers in Week 2. Hall handled 24 total touches to open the year, finishing with 118 total yards and a touchdown-an encouraging start under new OC Frank Reich. The Packers allowed just 3.7 yards per carry last week but did give up two rushing scores. Much of Hall's volume came in a favorable game script, something that may not repeat in Week 2, but with better than a 2:1 touch split with Braelon Allen, Hall will garner ample opportunity.

player.seasonOutlook: Hall received the franchise tag during the offseason and will return for his fifth season with the Jets. Having worked in the Jets' underwhelming offenses the past two years, Hall has struggled to finishes of 17th and 21st in fantasy points per game among RBs, which is a far cry from top-eight finishes during his first two seasons. Hall has remained busy, however, producing 266-plus touches each of the past three seasons. The 2022 second-round pick saw a dip in receiving work in 2025 (career-low 10% target share) but finished fourth in that category in both 2023 and 2024, so a rebound is possible with pocket QB Geno Smith now under center. Though the Jets' offense might continue to limit Hall's upside, the 25-year-old's combination of workload and talent positions him as a solid RB2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Malik Nabers looked spry in his first game of the season for the Giants, a Week 1 victory over the Cowboys. Nabers led the G-Men in targets with nine, en route to six catches for 69 yards in the 28-20 triumph. Nabers showed no ill effects from his torn ACL and meniscus suffered in Week 4 last season, only needing to get tackled by his new head coach John Harbaugh to prove he could take a hit before suiting up. In Week 2, Nabers will face a Rams defense that struggled against the pass in Week 1, allowing 205 passing yards and three passing scores in its season opener. Nabers will likely be covered by all-pro cornerback Trent McDuffie, though.

player.seasonOutlook: Nabers is on the comeback trail after a torn ACL limited him to only four appearances last season. In 18 full games in his career, Nabers has a massive 35% target share (11.3 per game) and he's averaging 18.2 fantasy PPG. As a rookie, the 2024 sixth overall pick finished seventh or better among receivers in targets, receptions, yards and fantasy points despite missing two games and dealing with New York's offensive struggles. Nabers' massive target share allowed him a high floor, as he was a top-30 fantasy scorer in 13 of 15 games, including 10 straight to end the 2024 season. He essentially has a new quarterback (Jaxson Dart threw only three passes his way last season), a new coach (John Harbaugh), a new offensive playcaller (Matt Nagy) and is recovering from the knee, so there are a lot of variables here, but the 23-year-old still holds elite upside. A healthy Nabers should be valued as a mid-to-back-end WR1, but the potential for a slow start needs to be considered on draft day.

outlooksByWeek.2: Luther Burden will look to stay highly involved as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. While Week 1 was the highest-scoring game in NFL history, Burden and Chicago's pass-catching corps were overshadowed by a dominant ground game. The second-year wideout's five catches for 63 yards wasn't bad, but he definitely has potential to be more dominant moving forward. He'll take on a Minnesota defense that gave up a 6-147-2 receiving line to Christian Watson and 6-95-0 to Matthew Golden in Week 1.

player.seasonOutlook: Burden enters his second NFL season as one of the most popular breakout candidates in fantasy. The 2025 second-round pick played sparingly during most of his rookie season, but flashed elite efficiency when called upon, ranking in the top five among wide receivers in catch rate (77%), yards per target (10.8), RAC (7.3) and YPRR (2.9). Burden is obviously an unproven commodity (he has two career top-20 fantasy outings, after all), but with DJ Moore no longer on the roster, he's a lock for a larger role and very well could lead Chicago in targets. He could cost a pretty penny on draft day, but Burden, 22, is a fine WR3 target with upside for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jadarian Price is set for his second NFL start when Seattle travels to Arizona in Week 2. Price was efficient in his professional debut last Wednesday versus New England, rushing 10 times for 52 yards while catching both of his targets for six yards. George Holani was given eight carries in the win, which helped limit Price's workload. The split between the two going forward remains to be seen, but there's certainly a chance that Price's touches will increase as the season progresses. The Cardinals' run defense looked good against the Chargers in Week 1, holding Omarion Hampton to 43 yards on 12 carries.

player.seasonOutlook: Price was selected by the Seahawks with the No. 32 overall pick of April's draft. Price managed only 280 career carries while stuck behind Jeremiyah Love at Notre Dame, but he showed well, posting a 4.13 YAC (second best in this rookie class) and 3.6 forced missed tackle rate (third best). He wasn't a factor as a receiver, however, totaling 15 receptions in 41 games. Price has a path to an immediate feature role in Seattle's run-first offense, though he may eventually defer substantial work to Zach Charbonnet (ACL recovery). Value Price as a flex, though he should land on the weekly RB2 radar while Charbonnet is sidelined.

outlooksByWeek.2: Sam LaPorta should remain a big part of Detroit's offense in Week 2 at Buffalo. In Week 1 against the Saints, LaPorta's 5-48-0 receiving line put him second to Amon-Ra St. Brown in receiving yards while tying Jahmyr Gibbs for second in catches. The fourth-year tight end will face a Bills defense that allowed 14.4 PPR points to Texans tight ends this past Sunday, so he'll have plenty of opportunities to build on his season-opening performance.

player.seasonOutlook: LaPorta has settled in as one of the league's top tight ends, but the 2023 second-round pick simply hasn't been able to match the fantasy success he enjoyed as a rookie. Since posting an 86-889-10 receiving line in 17 games that first season, LaPorta has totaled a 100-1,215-10 line in 25 games over the past two seasons. LaPorta's 2025 campaign was cut short by a back injury, otherwise he was well on his way to his third straight top-10 fantasy campaign (he finished seventh in PPG). The 25-year-old joins Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams and Jahmyr Gibbs as the clear "Core Four" targets in a good, pass-friendly Detroit offense, and is thus a solid fantasy TE1.
