The result was a 35th-place finish in fantasy points, which ended a streak of six consecutive top 25s. Moore now heads to Buffalo with Khalil Shakir as his only roadblock to emerging as Josh Allen's No. 1 target in Buffalo's high-scoring offense. Still in his prime at age 29, Moore has the look of a fantasy WR3 with upside for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Joe Burrow and the Bengals travel to take on the Texans in Week 2. Burrow completed 25 of 35 passes for 254 yards with one TD and one INT, and he rushed five times for 20 yards in their season-opening win. Houston ranks 28th in fantasy points allowed per game (39.0) to QBs after Josh Allen torched them for 357 scrimmage yards and four TDs. Burrow will look to get Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins more involved after the receivers combined for 71 yards on just five catches.

player.seasonOutlook: Burrow will attempt to bounce back after injuries limited him to eight games in 2025. The 29-year-old has now missed at least six games in three of his six pro seasons, including two of his past three. Burrow was still a starting-caliber fantasy quarterback when active last season (top-12 scorer in five of his final six games), but his ceiling was limited by a near complete lack of rushing (41 yards on 14 carries). Burrow was a top-five scoring quarterback in each of his past two full seasons, and coach Zac Taylor cut back a bit on his extreme pass-heavy playcalling last season, so Burrow is best valued as more of a midrange QB1 than an elite option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jonathon Brooks is expected to operate as Carolina's No. 2 running back in the Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. Brooks received just four carries in the Week 1 loss, which is fewer than Chuba Hubbard (10) and AJ Dillon (five). However, all of Dillon's work came when the Panthers were down substantially in the fourth quarter. Brooks showed flashes of brilliance when on the field, most notably on a 48-yard catch and run. He could continue to take work from Hubbard as the season continues. However, he's in for a tough Week 2 matchup, with Atlanta allowing just 2.8 yards per rush attempt in Week 1, the best mark in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Brooks is hoping to get his career on track in 2026 after appearing in only one game since being drafted in the second round of the 2024 draft. Brooks spent most of his rookie season recovering from a torn ACL suffered while at the University of Texas. He returned in Week 12 and handled 12 touches in three games prior to retearing the same ACL and missing the entire 2025 season. Only 23 years old and skilled as a rusher and receiver, Brooks figures to eventually get his shot at a lead-back role in the pros. He's expected to battle for touches with Chuba Hubbard this season, so it's possible he quickly earns his way into a fantasy-relevant role. Consider him in the middle rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyle Pitts will look to rebound for a disappointing Week 1 performance in the Falcons' Week 2 matchup against the Panthers. Pitts failed to haul in his lone target during last week's loss, with Bijan Robinson and Drake London combining for a 73.6% of Cooper Rush's targets. Despite this, Pitts could very well rebound against a Panthers defense that just allowed a whopping 59 points in Week 1, as they also gave up 11.5 PPR fantasy points to tight ends. His rebound could depend on Atlanta's quarterback situation, with both Michael Penix (knee) and Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) looking to return from injury in Week 2.

player.seasonOutlook: Right when it seemed like Pitts might never live up to the hype, the 2021 No. 4 pick put together the best season of his career. Pitts finished second among tight ends in routes, targets, catches, yards and fantasy points, setting career highs in all but the yardage category. He scored five touchdowns and has increased his total in that category (by exactly one) each season in the league. Pitts did a big chunk of his damage with Kirk Cousins under center (some with WR Drake London sidelined), which is notable as Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr. are set to battle for the Atlanta QB job. There's some obvious risk here considering Pitts finished 17th or lower in PPG three straight seasons before 2025, but he nonetheless enters his age-25 season as a priority target in the Atlanta offense. Consider him a midrange TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: RJ Harvey's workload was limited in the Broncos' season-opening loss to Kansas City. He gained 18 rushing yards on three carries and caught all four of his targets for 23 yards. That volume was comparable to J.K. Dobbins, who got eight touches-all carries-to Harvey's seven. Turnovers and game flow played a part in limiting their opportunities. Harvey's role as the primary pass-catching back still bodes well for his production in his second NFL season after posting a 47-356-5 line on 58 targets over 17 regular-season games in 2025. He'll get a potentially tough matchup in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that ranked third in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.

player.seasonOutlook: Harvey will go into his sophomore campaign looking to overtake J.K. Dobbins as Denver's lead back. In the 10 games in which both backs were active last season, Harvey handled 50 carries (20% team share) and 29 targets (9%), compared to Dobbins' 153 carries (60%) and 15 targets (4%). With Dobbins sidelined for the team's remaining nine games (including the playoff run), Harvey handled 115 carries (55%) and 41 targets (13%). He averaged 10.0 fantasy points with Dobbins and 14.2 without, though his 3.3 yards per carry during the final nine games was very poor. The entire Denver backfield is set to return in 2026, so similar deployment (which would include receiving specialist Tyler Badie) could be in the cards, though fourth-round rookie Jonah Coleman could factor in eventually as well. Harvey, 25, has a slight bit of breakout potential, but the committee setup suggests he's safest viewed as no more than a flex.

This already highly regarded defense only got stronger in June with the acquisition of two-time Defensive Player of the Year (2023, 2025) Myles Garrett. He wasn't their only addition, as CBs Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson were brought in from the Chiefs. Expect another productive season from this unit, though it does face one of the tougher early-season schedules, with the 49ers (Week 1), Broncos (3), Eagles (4) and Bills (5) among their first five opponents. The Rams' second-half schedule is one of the easiest, meaning they might be a better in-season trade target than a draft-day pickup.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rashid Shaheed will look to bounce back from a quiet season-opening performance when Seattle visits Arizona in Week 2. Shaheed caught just one of three targets for four yards against New England in Week 1. Drew Lock played most of that game behind center for the Seahawks after Sam Darnold (glute) made an early injury exit, and Lock figures to again lead the offense against Arizona. The Cardinals gave up just 14 points in a surprising victory over the Chargers last weekend, though they did allow Los Angeles' No. 1 wideout Ladd McConkey to put up a 5-82-1 line in under three quarters of action before he exited with a rib injury.

player.seasonOutlook: Shaheed re-signed with Seattle after the team acquired him at last year's trade deadline. Known primarily for his elite return ability, Shaheed made an impact at times as a receiver with New Orleans, but wasn't used much on offense after the trade. In 12 games with the Seahawks (including the playoffs), Shaheed cleared three touches in only two games and averaged 5.9 fantasy PPG. The team's financial investment in Shaheed suggests his role will expand in 2026, but he still has to fend off Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Cooper Kupp and second-year WR Tory Horton for snaps and targets. Shaheed enters his age-28 season yet to deliver a top-35 fantasy campaign, and he's unlikely to get there this season while also focusing on special teams and working in Seattle's low-pass-volume offense.

outlooksByWeek.2: Baker Mayfield will look to rebound from a tough Week 1 performance in Tampa Bay's Week 2 matchup against the Browns. Mayfield threw for 216 yards while adding a rushing touchdown last week, but he fumbled three times and struggled to finish drives. He should be in for a very favorable Week 2 matchup against a Browns defense that allowed 28.3 fantasy points to quarterbacks and four passing touchdowns in Week 1. If Mayfield isn't able to respond with a solid fantasy performance in a clear revenge game, there could be doubts about his reliability moving forward.

player.seasonOutlook: Mayfield is back for Year 4 as Tampa Bay's starting quarterback. He has put together three consecutive top-12 fantasy campaigns, though his 2025 season (12th in total points, but 19th in points per game) was a big step back from 2024 (fourth overall and per game). Mayfield tossed 26 touchdowns (way down from 41 in 2024) and severely lacked upside, managing only four top-10 fantasy weeks. Granted, the 31-year-old was not fully healthy throughout the season and did still finish in the top 10 at the position in key categories, including passing yards, passing TDs and rushing yards. With a solid supporting cast and Zac Robinson as playcaller, Mayfield has some rebound potential and does just enough with his legs to make him an appealing QB2 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jalen McMillan (knee) will operate as one of the Buccaneers' top receiving options if active for the Week 2 matchup against the Browns. McMillan was unable to suit up in Week 1 due to a nagging knee injury, but he could have a valuable role in Tampa Bay's receiving corps once healthy. Outside of Emeka Egbuka, the Buccaneers' wideouts combined to catch seven of eight targets for 76 yards in Week 1, which suggests McMillan will have a large opportunity to contribute when available. He's in for a great Week 2 matchup as well, with Cleveland's defense allowing three touchdowns to WRs last week.

player.seasonOutlook: McMillan is a fascinating late-round sleeper after he impressed as a rookie before missing all but four games due to injury last season. The 2024 third-round pick was featured during the final five games of his rookie season and exploded for a league-high seven TD catches (at least one in all five outings) and 19.8 fantasy PPG (more than 16.7 points in all five) in that span. He was limited in his return to action late in 2025, but did flash with a 7-114-0 performance on nine targets in Week 17. The 24-year-old has a path to a near-every-down role in 2026 with only Emeka Egbuka and 30-year-old Chris Godwin ahead of him on the depth chart. McMillan is worth the inexpensive flier on draft day.

outlooksByWeek.2: Isiah Pacheco will miss Week 2 as the Lions travel to Buffalo. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he recently underwent surgery. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return in jeopardy. He's currently expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will handle whatever RB2 duties are available behind Jahmyr Gibbs.

player.seasonOutlook: Pacheco signed with Detroit in the offseason after a four-year stint with the Chiefs. The 2022 seventh-round NFL draft pick opened his pro career with a bang, totaling 2,139 yards and 14 touchdowns on 432 touches during his first two seasons (31 games). Injuries and a big drop in efficiency have limited him to 952 yards and three TDs on 232 touches over the past two seasons (20 games) and ultimately led to his exit from Kansas City. The 27-year-old will now get a shot to replace David Montgomery as Detroit's change-of-pace back to Jahmyr Gibbs. Pacheco might hit for the occasional touchdown, but he won't have standalone fantasy value unless Gibbs misses time. Consider Pacheco a late-round insurance flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: T.J. Hockenson will look to build off a solid Week 1 performance as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Hockenson was second in targets against the Packers behind Justin Jefferson, reeling in four of five targets for 36 yards and a touchdown. The veteran tight end was a go-to outlet for veteran Carson Wentz, and he could continue to be one no matter who lines up under center moving forward. He'll take on a Bears defense that allowed a middle-of-the-pack 11.5 PPR points to Carolina tight ends in a high-scoring season opener.

player.seasonOutlook: It's been a rough go for Hockenson since he peaked with a 95-960-5 receiving line in 2023. He tore an ACL in Week 16 that season and was limited to a 41-455-0 receiving line upon his return in 10 games in 2024. A bounce-back was expected in 2025, but Hockenson handled a weak 16% target share (his lowest since he was a rookie in 2019) and couldn't overcome the team's QB woes en route to a 51-438-3 showing. Hockenson has now followed four straight top-seven fantasy PPG seasons with finishes of 17th and 26th. The 29-year-old could very well get back on track in 2026, but he'll need solid play from Kyler Murray. Hockenson is a fringe TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cairo Santos will aim to stay perfect as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Santos was on the field a lot in Week 1 against the Panthers, but most of his 11 points came from his eight PATs. The veteran kicker could continue to benefit from a high-scoring offense, and he'll look to continue against a Minnesota squad that allowed three field goals and an extra point to Trey Smack this past Sunday.

Bijan Robinson will continue to lead Atlanta's offense in a Week 2 divisional matchup against the Panthers. Robinson received a whopping 29 touches in Week 1, tying Ashton Jeanty for the second-most in the NFL. The Texas product looked explosive despite the Falcons' offensive struggles, which is a good sign for his outlook going forward. Robinson is in for a great matchup as well, with the Panthers defense allowing 291 rushing yards and six rushing touchdowns in a Week 1 loss to the Bears.

player.seasonOutlook: Robinson enters his fourth season having finished in the top five among running backs in carries, rushing yards, touches, yards and fantasy points in each of the past two seasons. Also a big factor as a receiver, he has ranked no lower than fifth at the position in routes, targets, receptions and receiving yards in his three pro seasons. In 2025, PFF tracked him with 86 forced missed tackles, which was easily the most among backs. The 24-year-old is in his prime and, though he has a new coach in Kevin Stefanski, his path to a massive offensive role remains clear. He's on the short list of players who should be considered with the first pick of your fantasy draft.

outlooksByWeek.2: Trey McBride marches into a Week 2 matchup versus Seattle fresh off a strong season-opening performance in Arizona's victory against the Chargers. McBride led Cardinals pass catchers across the board with nine catches, 13 targets and 95 yards in that win, and he scored the team's lone passing touchdown. The All-Pro is essentially matchup-proof as possibly the league's premier tight end, though he'll draw a tough Seahawks defense in Week 2. However, it's worth noting that Seattle gave up the sixth-most receiving yards to tight ends during the regular season last year.

player.seasonOutlook: McBride has emerged as one of the league's top pass catchers -- not just tight ends -- as he trails only Ja'Marr Chase in targets (317) and receptions (252) over the past two seasons and is sixth in receiving yards (2,385). McBride led the tight end position in every fantasy-relevant counting stat in 2025, and his league-high 15 top-12 fantasy weeks were six more than any other player at the position. He finished third in the NFL with 17 end zone targets. McBride really thrived when Jacoby Brissett (21.1 PPG) replaced Kyler Murray (12.5) under center, which only adds to his 2026 appeal. The 26-year-old should be on your radar at the first-/second-round turn.

outlooksByWeek.2: Travis Etienne is expected to remain New Orleans' top running back in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Despite Alvin Kamara (knee) being sidelined for the Week 1 overtime loss, Etienne only received nine carries, tying Kendre Miller for the most on the team. However, Etienne was busy as a receiver, catching seven of nine targets for 46 yards, which is a positive sign for his fantasy outlook going forward. He could be in for another productive week, as Baltimore's defense allowed 28.1 PPR fantasy points to running backs in Week 1.

player.seasonOutlook: Etienne signed with the Saints after spending the first five seasons of his pro career with the Jaguars. The 2021 first-round pick has produced at least 1,399 scrimmage yards in three of the past four seasons and scored a career-high 13 touchdowns in 2025. A capable rusher and receiver, Etienne has already reached 1,000-plus rushing yards three times and has 35-plus catches in each of the past four seasons. Even if the Saints retain Alvin Kamara as a situational player, Etienne will have a clear path to feature-back duties in an ascending offense led by second-year QB Tyler Shough. That will be enough to position the 27-year-old for his third top-15 fantasy campaign in four years. Consider Etienne a solid RB2 target with backend RB1 upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Drake Maye will hope to clean up mistakes when the Patriots host the Steelers in Week 2. Maye threw three interceptions in the season opener while under constant pressure, and Pittsburgh's defense, led by T.J. Watt, recorded four sacks last week. While the chemistry was still developing, Maye is now also without No. 1 WR A.J. Brown (ankle) for the immediate future, leading to questionable receiving options. While Maye remains a dangerous runner that will keep his floor reasonable, this likely low-scoring game may not be ideal for a true bounce-back performance.

player.seasonOutlook: Maye is entering his third NFL season and second full season as New England's starter. The 2024 No. 3 draft pick is fresh off a breakout 2025 campaign in which he finished in the top five among quarterbacks in pass completions, yards and TDs, as well as rush attempts and yards. Maye, who led the league in completion percentage (72%) and yards per attempt (8.9), trailed only Josh Allen in fantasy points (351.9), fantasy points per game (20.7) and top-10 fantasy weeks (10). The NFL MVP runner-up will need to overcome a tougher schedule, but he has a better supporting cast (including A.J. Brown) and the 24-year-old's combination of passing talent and rushing ability have him well positioned for another top-five fantasy campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: Carnell Tate tied for the team lead in receiving yards during his NFL debut, but he had just 38 yards on six targets as Titans QB Cam Ward threw for a meager 140 yards. Tennessee's passing game is likely to struggle again in Week 2 against Philadelphia's excellent secondary, led by cornerback Quinyon Mitchell. Tate is likely to maintain a prominent role on the rebuilding Titans after being drafted fourth overall out of Ohio State, but the rookie WR is hard to trust as anything more than a fantasy WR3 or flex play until Tennessee's offense shows some life.

player.seasonOutlook: Tate was selected by the Titans with the fourth overall pick of April's draft. He didn't see a ton of volume at Ohio State, but he was efficient, averaging 13.1 yards per target (first in this rookie WR class) and 3.06 yards per route run (third) in 2025. He also paced the class in YPT for his career (11.6) and caught an impressive 75% of his targets during the 39-game span. Tate underwhelmed in the 40-yard dash at the combine (4.53 at 192 pounds), but he measured in with big hands and a large wingspan. Wide receivers selected in the top 10 handle, on average, one-quarter of their team's targets and generally deliver WR2/3 fantasy production. Cam Ward's development will be key here, but Tate's combination of talent and projected target volume is enough to make him an appealing WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Alec Pierce led the Colts with 61 receiving yards in the season opener despite battling a heel injury heading into the game. In addition, he left during the first half to get X-rays on his hand and wrist after hitting a defender's helmet. His practice participation is likely to be affected by those injuries, but Pierce is seemingly on track to suit up in Week 2 against the Chiefs and can be viewed as a solid WR3 or flex option. He brings big-play ability to an otherwise underwhelming Colts passing game, averaging at least 21.3 yards per catch in each of the past two seasons and leading the team with 1,003 receiving yards in 2025.

player.seasonOutlook: Pierce has spent the majority of his first four NFL seasons as a situational deep threat, but that didn't stop him from becoming one of the league's highest-paid wide receivers during the offseason. The 2022 second-round pick is fresh off a career year and he's now paced all receivers in YPR, YPT and aDOT each of the last two seasons. However, he's yet to finish a season better than 48th at WR in target share (18%), 42nd in targets (84), 45th in catches (47), 18th in yards (1,003), 18th in TDs (seven) or 25th in fantasy PPG. Of course, with Michael Pittman Jr. no longer in the mix, Pierce is a good bet for a more well-rounded role as Daniel Jones' top target. There's some risk here, but the 26-year-old's hefty contract suggests we should take him seriously as a fantasy WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Michael Pittman and the Steelers travel for a Week 2 tilt against the Patriots. The former Indianapolis Colt secured all three targets for a team-high 58 yards in his debut for Pittsburgh. Pittman finished sixth in targets but still did plenty of damage with his opportunities, and if the Steelers want to throw the ball 40-plus times a game, he could develop into a reliable fantasy receiver. New England's defense ranks 21st in receiving yards allowed to WRs (161), but they will be playing at home with a rest advantage.

player.seasonOutlook: Pittman was traded to the Steelers after spending his first six NFL seasons with the Colts. The 2020 second-round pick handled a hefty 23.6% of Indianapolis' targets during his tenure, which helped him to four top-20 fantasy campaigns. Pittman has reached 800 receiving yards in five consecutive seasons while primarily operating as a short-to-intermediate target. The role has limited his scoring (he has 25 TDs in 95 games) and that may not change much with DK Metcalf on the other side in Pittsburgh. Of course, Pittman will be a featured target in an offense led by Aaron Rodgers. That's enough to put the 28-year-old squarely in the weekly WR3 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: Deebo Samuel will look to build upon a strong season-opening performance when the 49ers face Miami in Week 2. In Samuel's return to San Francisco following a one-year hiatus, he caught six of seven targets for 48 yards and a touchdown in last Thursday's win over the Rams. Samuel and Mike Evans finished with nearly identical receiving lines, suggesting that both veteran wideouts can thrive with QB Brock Purdy. The Dolphins were beat handily by the Raiders in Week 1 while giving up three TDs through the air (though two were to RB Ashton Jeanty).

player.seasonOutlook: Samuel reunited with the 49ers in July after solid yet unspectacular lone season in Washington. The former second-round pick cleared 85 touches and 800 scrimmage yards for the fifth consecutive season and finished 25th among receivers in fantasy points -- his third-career top-30 fantasy campaign. Samuel's role as a short-area target and occasional rusher gets the ball in his hands plenty (he's ranked in the top 15 among WRs in touches and RAC five years in a row), but it doesn't allow him much scoring upside (10 TDs over the last two years, and he's never cleared five end zone targets in one season). Now 30 years old, Samuel figures to resume his role as a short-area playmaker in Kyle Shanahan's highly-efficient offense. He's a fine late-round flier with WR3/flex upside.

Jacobs' 2025 season can be split in two parts: pre-injury and post-injury. While healthy during his first nine games, Jacobs picked up where he left off from a terrific 2024 debut season with Green Bay, averaging 21.1 touches and 19.6 fantasy points while scoring 11 TDs. After missing all but 11 snaps during Weeks 11 and 12, Jacobs returned and wasn't quite the same, averaging 14.6 touches and 11.3 points while totaling three touchdowns in his final five games. But Jacobs, 28, was still effective overall (PFF's fourth-highest-graded back) and has a clear grasp on lead-back duties in a good Green Bay offense that has afforded him 30 touchdowns (fifth most in the NFL) in 32 games. He's a fine back-end RB1 when active, but a likely suspension makes him less valuable on draft day.He's worth a mid-round flier until the dust settles.

outlooksByWeek.2: Alvin Kamara (knee) is expected to serve as one of the Saints' top running backs if active for the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Kamara was sidelined for Week 1 but is expected to return for Week 2, likely operating as the Saints' top receiving back. He could take work away from Travis Etienne, who caught seven of eight targets in last week's overtime loss. Tyler Shough attempted 56 passes in Week 1, which bodes well for Kamara's potential upside as a receiver. He's in for a solid Week 2 matchup as well, with the Ravens defense giving up 5.3 yards per touch to RBs in Week 1.

player.seasonOutlook: Kamara is entering his age-31 season set to play a change-of-pace role behind Travis Etienne and is unlikely to be a fantasy option. Over the past seven seasons, only two backs age 31 or older have posted a top-30 fantasy campaign, and both required 16-plus touchdowns. (Kamara hasn't cleared nine TDs since 2020 and scored once in 2025). Injuries limited Kamara to career-low marks across the board last season (including a 10% target share, considerably worse than his previous career low of 18%), and he hasn't played a full season since his rookie year (2017). A longtime fantasy star, Kamara is worth no more than a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Romeo Doubs will seek a larger role in the Patriots' passing game in Week 2 against the Steelers. Doubs failed to record a catch on three targets in his team debut, playing only 56% of the snaps despite New England losing A.J. Brown to a high-ankle sprain. With Brown set to miss significant time, Doubs should garner more opportunities, but it looks as though he's still developing chemistry with Drake Maye. Questions remain regarding the Steelers' secondary, which is likely to remain without Joey Porter Jr. They weren't tested last week, but counting on a breakthrough from Doubs is risky.

player.seasonOutlook: Doubs signed with the Patriots during free agency after spending his first four NFL seasons with the Packers. He was a serviceable player during his Green Bay tenure, but he never finished a season in the top 30 among receivers in targets, catches, yards or fantasy points. Consistently mediocre, Doubs has averaged either 10.2 or 10.3 fantasy PPG each of the last three seasons. In New England, Doubs is likely to settle in as Drake Maye's No. 2 target behind A.J. Brown, though his target ceiling figures to be capped with the likes of DeMario Douglas, Mack Hollins and Kyle Williams also in the mix at receiver. Doubs, 26, is a fine addition to your bench, but his upside is limited.

The No. 1 D/ST selected on average last season, the Steelers finished a disappointing 14th in fantasy points and scored fewer than five points in 8-of-17 games. They've since overhauled their coaching staff, with Mike McCarthy replacing Mike Tomlin, and Patrick Graham as defensive coordinator, the same role he held with the Raiders from 2022-25. The offseason additions of S Jaquan Brisker and CB Jamel Dean should bolster this unit, and it benefits greatly from one of the softest September and October schedules in the league. Get this D/ST early, but be prepared to seek a replacement after that point.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brian Robinson is expected to operate as the Falcons' No. 2 running back in the Week 2 matchup against the Panthers. Despite playing behind Bijan Robinson, Brian Robinson could have material fantasy value this week, as Carolina's defense allowed 291 rushing yards and six touchdowns in Week 1. Additionally, Robinson received nine carries in the Week 1 loss to the Steelers, which is solid volume for a complementary role. He could find value with the Panthers giving up 52.8 PPR fantasy points to the running back position last week.

player.seasonOutlook: After a one-year stint as Christian McCaffrey's backup in San Francisco, Robinson signed with Atlanta where he'll now operate as a change-of-pace back behind Bijan Robinson. The 2022 third-round pick soaked up 200-plus touches in each of his first three NFL seasons (all with Washington) prior to dipping to 100 touches in 2025. Robinson is a big back who can handle early-down and short-yardage work, but he's not much of a factor as a receiver (92 career targets). He's yet to post a top-20 fantasy campaign and he won't come close to that in 2026 unless Bijan Robinson suffers a major injury. The 27-year-old back is no more than a solid insurance stash.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kayshon Boutte was held to one catch in his Texans debut, so he doesn't profile as a viable fantasy option for Week 2 against the Bengals. Boutte may still be learning the playbook after being acquired in an Aug. 24 trade from New England, and facing a tough Buffalo secondary didn't help things in Week 1, but he will need to demonstrate greater involvement in the game plan to warrant lineup consideration outside the deepest of formats. Cincinnati's secondary played well in Week 1, as no Buccaneers WR exceeded 63 yards against them.

player.seasonOutlook: Boutte was traded to the Texans in August. Reportedly a cut/trade candidate throughout most of the 2025 offseason, Boutte went on to lead the AFC champion Patriots' wide receiver room in routes and touchdowns while playing 67% of the offensive snaps when active. Despite the generous usage in a good offense, Boutte wasn't a reliable fantasy option, averaging 8.9 fantasy PPG. After seeing a career-high nine targets in Week 1, Boutte didn't clear five in a game the rest of the regular season. The 2023 sixth-round pick has finished in the range of 500-600 yards each of the last two seasons and has yet to produce a top-50 fantasy campaign. Now with Houston, Boutte will compete with Xavier Hutchinson and Jaylin Noel for Houston's No. 2 receiver role behind Nico Collins. Even if he wins that job, he doesn't figure to see enough work to find his way into the weekly flex discussion.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chase McLaughlin will look to remain perfect in the Buccaneers' Week 2 matchup against the Browns. McLaughlin made all five of his kicks during last week's loss, including a 51-yard field goal. With the Browns defense allowing 34 total points and 10 kicking points in a Week 1 loss, McLaughlin is likely in for lots more scoring opportunities in Week 2.

Chris Brooks will remain in the backfield mix for Green Bay against the Jets in Week 2. While Brooks took an ancillary role to Marshawn Lloyd in Week 1, Brooks still finished the game with seven rushes for 29 yards to Lloyd's 13 for 37. Brooks is also an excellent pass blocker, so he'll still get time on the field even if it doesn't convert to rushing attempts. New York dominated Tennessee in the trenches in Week 1, but they should be a lot less daunting than a staunch Minnesota front.
